label: Concept by key
summary: The game concept with the given key, as text.
details: Vanilla wraps it as [ConceptByKey('$KEY|q$')|E] in localization, for example for a title tier or a combat phase, so the text it gives is shown as a concept link (the |E format). Going by this use, the argument is the key of a game concept.

label: Copy build info
summary: Going by its name, copies the game's build and version information to the clipboard.
details: Going by its name and its single use, vanilla attaches it to a click (onclick) in the front-end loading screen. It returns nothing, it only acts.

label: Copy server ID
summary: Copies the server ID of the current multiplayer session to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla uses it on a click in the in-game menu and, as LobbyView.CopyServerID, in the multiplayer lobby. It returns nothing.

label: Holds coronations
summary: Whether the given character is one who will hold coronations.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'coronation_trigger_gui' with the character as its root. Vanilla uses it inside the create-title texts, together with a check for the coronations DLC feature.

label: Coronation reward progress text
summary: Gives the second text only while the activity's special progress is below the given value.
details: The game's documentation says it checks the current progress. The macro compares the activity window's special progress value with the first argument and shows the second argument (a localization key) when progress is lower. Vanilla uses it with 25, 50 and 75 for the bar segments of the coronation activity.

fields.name: SetVariable
fields.text: The progress value to compare against.

fields.name: SetVariable2
fields.text: The localization key of the text to show.

label: Coronation decision timer text
summary: Gives the second text unless the detail view of the given decision is currently shown.
details: The game's documentation says it checks the cooldown in the decision's title. The macro itself adds the second text (a localization key) when the decision's detail is not shown. Vanilla uses it in the oath action labels, with a decision key and a matching timer text key.

fields.name: SetVariable2
fields.text: The localization key of the text to add.

label: Council owner can use vizier
summary: Whether the owner of the shown council has a government that may appoint viziers.
details: The macro checks the government flag 'may_appoint_viziers' on the shown council's owner. The game's documentation describes it as a clan government check, but the flag is what is tested. Vanilla uses it in the council window to show or hide parts of the window.

label: Council owner has vizier
summary: Whether the owner of the shown council has a vizier on their council.
details: The macro looks at the 'councillor_vizier' position of the council window and checks that its active task has a valid councillor. Vanilla uses it in the council window to show or hide parts of the window.

label: Council owner is nomadic
summary: Whether the owner of the shown council has a nomadic government.
details: The macro checks the government flag 'government_is_nomadic' on the council's owner. Vanilla uses it in the council window to show or hide parts of the window.

label: Create command popup
summary: Creates a command popup for the given command object.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it takes a command that the game offers, such as abandoning a ruler objective, creating a herder for a title or rebuilding a great building, and is used on clicks. It returns nothing. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The command to put in the popup.
fields.values: a command object from the GUI

label: Progress percent
summary: The progress of a current whole number towards a maximum, as a percentage from 0 to 100.
details: The result is limited to the range 0 to 100. Vanilla uses it as the value of progress bars, for example for inspirations and the ruler designer's points.

label: Date
summary: The date a game text is about, such as the current date or a start date.
details: Vanilla uses it in about 100 lines and writes it out as text, for example "Current date: ..." and "Started on ...". The game calls it a Jomini Date (the date type of its engine).

label: Latest date
summary: The later end of a date range in a game text.
details: Vanilla's one use writes a range as "[DATE_MIN] - [DATE_MAX]" in short date form. DATE_MIN is the earlier end.

label: Earliest date
summary: The earlier end of a date range in a game text.
details: Vanilla's one use writes a range as "[DATE_MIN] - [DATE_MAX]" in short date form. DATE_MAX is the later end.

label: Decision
summary: The decision a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the decision's title as a given character sees it, for example when a decision's cooldown is removed.

label: Defender
summary: A character object that a text can work with, named 'defender'.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for the defending character. The two vanilla lines found do not call it: they write 'DEFENDER' as a text key inside SelectLocalization, so they do not show how the function is used.

label: Doctrine
summary: The faith doctrine a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to say which doctrine a faith gains, with its group's name, both written for that faith. OTHER_DOCTRINE_TYPE is the doctrine it replaces.

label: Domicile
summary: The domicile (a character's own property that acts as their power base instead of holdings) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to reach the domicile's owner, for example "[owner] gains ... provisions".

label: Domicile building
summary: The kind of domicile building a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's building tooltips use it for the building's name, its description and the description of its effect.

label: Domicile type
summary: The kind of domicile a game text is about.
details: Vanilla builds a domicile's name from it, after the owner's house name or the title's name ("[house] [domicile type]").

label: Dynasty
summary: The dynasty a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name the dynasty, for example when it gains a modifier.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to name the house, for example when it gains a modifier. In house relation texts it is the first house and DYNASTY_HOUSE_2 the second.

label: Second house
summary: The second dynasty house in a text about two houses.
details: Vanilla uses it in house relation texts, after DYNASTY_HOUSE: a relation's name ("[house]-[house 2]") and the text that a relation is set up between the two.

label: Dynasty legacy
summary: A dynasty legacy object that a text can work with.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for a dynasty legacy a text is about. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Dynasty perk
summary: The dynasty perk a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name a dynasty perk that is gained or lost.

label: First items of a list
summary: The first few items of a list of the interface.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it cuts a list (a data model) down to its first N items. Vanilla uses it for lists of DLCs and of activity characters, with counts such as 10, 15 and 3. The game gives no return type for it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list to take items from.

label: List has items
summary: Whether a list of the interface contains at least one item.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is true when the list is not empty. Vanilla uses it to show parts of a window and to choose between texts, for example for a title's line of succession or the enabled DLCs.

label: Join list into text
summary: Goes through the items of a list and joins them into one text, each shown through a localization key.
details: The item key is used for each item and the separator key goes between them (the order the vanilla lines show). Inside those texts, ITEM_INDEX holds the current position and IS_LAST_ITEM is 1 for the last item or separator. Vanilla uses it to list the faiths an artifact is sanctified for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The localization key used for each item.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The localization key used between items.

label: Last items of a list
summary: The last few items of a list of the interface.
details: Going by its name and the matching DataModelFirst, it keeps the last N items. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list to take items from.

label: List without first items
summary: A list of the interface with its first items left out.
details: Going by its name and its uses, the second value is how many items to skip. Vanilla uses it on map icon lists, for example skipping one project or skipping past the first valid domicile.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list to take items from.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: How many items to skip at the start.

label: List without last items
summary: A list of the interface with its last items left out.
details: Going by its name and its uses, the second value is how many items to drop at the end. Vanilla uses it with 1, for example on planned activity phases and event options.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list to take items from.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: How many items to drop at the end.

label: Part of a list
summary: A part of a list of the interface.
details: Going by its name and its two uses, it takes a part of the list, given by two numbers. Vanilla uses it to show part of the scoreboard and entrants in the imperial examination, with 3 as the second value. The exact meaning of the two numbers is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list to take items from.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: Probably how long the stretch is.

label: Days per month
summary: The average number of days in a month, which is 30.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the lines found. It returns a whole number.

label: Days per week
summary: The number of days in a week.
details: Vanilla uses it in the activity window, as the max value of an element and as an argument of GetTicksSinceLastProgress. It returns a whole number.

label: Days per year
summary: The number of days in a year, with no leap years.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the lines found. It returns a whole number.

label: Title shield offset
summary: The standard shift (0.0, 0.04) of a coat of arms inside the default title shield.
details: It is a shorthand for the 2D value 0.0,0.04, meant for the standard gfx/interface/coat_of_arms/title shields. Vanilla uses it as coat_of_arms_offset in the HUD and in the shared coat of arms widget.

label: Title shield scale
summary: The standard size factor (0.9, 0.9) of a coat of arms inside the default title shield.
details: It is a shorthand for the 2D value 0.9,0.9, meant for the standard gfx/interface/coat_of_arms/title shields. Vanilla uses it as coat_of_arms_scale in the HUD and in the shared coat of arms widget.

label: Default barter click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a barter mission.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is the click action for barter mission icons on the map, called with the mission itself. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The barter mission that was clicked.

label: Default character click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a character.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is the usual click action for character portraits in the HUD, the outliner and similar places, called with the character's ID. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the clicked character.

label: Default character right-click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a right-click on a character.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is the usual right-click action for characters in the outliner and on map icons, called with the character's ID. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the clicked character.

label: Default coat of arms click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a title's coat of arms.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with a title's ID, for example the player's primary title in the HUD. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the title whose coat of arms was clicked.

label: Default coat of arms right-click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a right-click on a title's coat of arms.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with a title's ID, in the outliner, the vassal detail window and the barter window. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the title whose coat of arms was clicked.

label: Default dynasty arms click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a dynasty's coat of arms.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with a dynasty's ID, in the character filter, the dynasty tree and the ledger. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the dynasty whose coat of arms was clicked.

label: Default house arms click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a dynasty house's coat of arms.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with a house's ID, in the HUD and the character filter. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the house whose coat of arms was clicked.

label: Default raid click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a raid.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is the click action of raid icons in the outliner and on the map, called with the raid itself. It returns nothing.

label: Default realm flag click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a realm's flag.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with a character's ID, on the map, in the character window and in the county view. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the character whose realm flag was clicked.

label: Default realm flag right-click
summary: Presumably the game's standard reaction to a right-click on a realm's flag.
details: Going by its name and the matching DefaultOnRealmFlagClick, it takes a character ID. Vanilla does not use it in the lines found, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the ID of the realm's ruler.

label: Default siege click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a siege.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is called with the siege's ID, in the outliner and on map icons. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ID of the siege that was clicked.

label: Default struggle phase click
summary: Runs the game's standard reaction to a click on a phase of a struggle.
details: Going by its name and its one use in the struggle window, it takes the struggle's ID and the phase. It returns nothing.

label: Divide fixed-point numbers
summary: The first fixed-point number divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, Arg0 is divided by Arg1. Vanilla uses it in the ledger to divide a prestige, piety or merit level by a fixed number (40 or 90) for an alpha value.

label: Divide 2D vectors
summary: The first 2D vector divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, the two values are 2D vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Divide 3D vectors
summary: The first 3D vector divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, the two values are 3D vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Divide 4D vectors
summary: The first 4D vector divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, the two values are 4D vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Divide decimals
summary: The first decimal number divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, Arg0 is divided by Arg1 and the result is a decimal number. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Divide whole numbers
summary: The first whole number divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, Arg0 is divided by Arg1 and the result is a whole number. How it rounds is not documented. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Divide unsigned numbers
summary: The first non-negative whole number divided by the second.
details: Going by its name, the values are unsigned whole numbers (0 and up). How it rounds is not documented. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Double to decimal
summary: Going by its name, the given high-precision decimal number turned into an ordinary decimal number.
details: Its one use, in the engine's entity editor, passes the running animation's current time and shows the result as a value. The game documents nothing more.

label: Epidemic
summary: The epidemic outbreak a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in epidemic effect and condition texts, for example when its outbreak intensity changes or to say in which province it began.

label: Epidemic type
summary: The kind of disease a game text is about, such as for a new outbreak.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts that a new outbreak appears: "[intensity] [type] outbreak appears in ...".

label: Culture era
summary: The culture era (a stage a culture must reach before it can discover that era's innovations) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's culture window uses it in the rules for researching innovations: an era must be reached first, and enough innovations of one era are needed for the next.

label: Contested legitimacy warning
summary: The short warning text about contested legitimacy when the given character creates the selected title.
details: It gives the warning for the highest tier that applies (tier 3, else 2, else 1) and an empty text when none applies. Vanilla appends it to the 'You will gain prestige and legitimacy' text when creating a title.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the title.
fields.values: a character from the GUI, such as GetPlayer

label: Contested legitimacy warning for title
summary: The short warning text about contested legitimacy when the given character creates a specific title.
details: Like EmpireFaithGateContestedLegitimacyWarning, it gives the warning for the highest tier that applies and an empty text otherwise, but for a title you name instead of the selected one. Vanilla uses it in the create-title tooltip.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the title.

fields.name: TargetTitle
fields.text: The title that would be created.

label: Gains contested legitimacy tier 1
summary: Whether creating the selected empire would apply the tier 1 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_1' with the character as root and the selected title as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the empire.

label: Tier 1 legitimacy on title
summary: Whether creating a specific title would apply the tier 1 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_1' with the character as root and the title you give as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the title.

fields.name: TargetTitle
fields.text: The title that would be created.

label: Gains contested legitimacy tier 2
summary: Whether creating the selected empire would apply the tier 2 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_2' with the character as root and the selected title as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the empire.

label: Tier 2 legitimacy on title
summary: Whether creating a specific title would apply the tier 2 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_2' with the character as root and the title you give as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the title.

fields.name: TargetTitle
fields.text: The title that would be created.

label: Gains contested legitimacy tier 3
summary: Whether creating the selected empire would apply the tier 3 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_3' with the character as root and the selected title as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the empire.

label: Tier 3 legitimacy on title
summary: Whether creating a specific title would apply the tier 3 contested legitimacy modifier.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'empire_faith_gate_contested_warning_3' with the character as root and the title you give as 'landed_title'. Vanilla does not use it directly in the lines found.

fields.name: TargetCharacter
fields.text: The character who would create the title.

fields.name: TargetTitle
fields.text: The title that would be created.

label: Empty scope
summary: An empty starting point for a text that needs no character or title.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 1200 lines, mostly to read a named script value in a text without a character or title behind it:`[EmptyScope.ScriptValue('...')]`, for example a feast's cost discount as a percentage.

label: Equal fixed-point numbers
summary: Whether two fixed-point numbers are equal.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts to choose between two wordings, for example to highlight a scheme's success chance when it equals the maximum.

label: Equal 2D vectors
summary: Whether two 2D vectors are equal.
details: Going by its name, it compares the two vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Equal 3D vectors
summary: Whether two 3D vectors are equal.
details: Going by its name, it compares the two vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Equal 4D vectors
summary: Whether two 4D vectors are equal.
details: Going by its name, it compares the two vectors. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Equal decimals
summary: Whether two decimal numbers are equal.
details: Going by its name, it compares the two numbers. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Equal whole numbers
summary: Whether two whole numbers are equal.
details: Vanilla uses it a great deal in texts and windows to choose between wordings or to show parts of a window, for example in the activity and court grandeur texts.

label: Equal texts
summary: Whether two texts are exactly the same.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts to compare names, for example a holy site's type name with its own name, or an innovation's name with its type's name.

label: Equal unsigned numbers
summary: Whether two non-negative whole numbers are equal.
details: Vanilla uses it to compare IDs, for example whether a title's nominee is a given character in the cardinals window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, 0 or more, such as an ID

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a whole number, 0 or more, such as an ID

label: Error tooltip
summary: A text describing an error, for use as a tooltip.
details: Going by its name and its single use, it is set as the tooltip of a shared interface component. The game documents nothing more.

label: Run console command
summary: Runs one console command, given as text.
details: Vanilla's console window uses it to run script files, for example 'run run.txt'. It returns nothing. Commands to run several at once are ExecuteConsoleCommands and ExecuteConsoleCommandsForced.

label: Run console commands
summary: Runs several console commands one after the other, and stops at the first one that fails.
details: The commands are written in one text, separated by ';'. Compare ExecuteConsoleCommandsForced, which carries on after a failure. Vanilla does not use it in the lines found.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a text with commands separated by ';'

label: Run console commands anyway
summary: Runs several console commands one after the other, and carries on even if one fails.
details: The commands are written in one text, separated by ';'. Compare ExecuteConsoleCommands, which stops at the first failure. Vanilla does not use it in the lines found.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a text with commands separated by ';'

label: Faction
summary: The faction a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name the faction when it gains or loses discontent or is disbanded.

label: Faith
summary: The faith a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 200 lines, for example as the faith a scheme is started against, and as the faith that doctrine names are written for.

label: Focus
summary: The lifestyle focus a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the message that a focus is no longer valid and in the lifestyle window's tooltip, which shows the focus's description and effects.

label: Founder
summary: The character who founded something a text names, such as a holy order.
details: Vanilla builds holy order names from it, using the founder's culture or house ("[culture] Order", "[house] Order").

label: Factor to multiplier
summary: Turns a factor such as 1.25 into a multiplier such as 0.25 by subtracting 1.
details: Vanilla does not use it in the lines found.

label: Fixed-point to decimal
summary: Converts a fixed-point number into a decimal number (float).
details: Vanilla uses it to feed progress bars and values, for example a domicile's construction progress times 100, an artifact's maximum durability and the combat advantage.

label: Fixed-point to whole number
summary: Converts a fixed-point number into a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts, for example to turn an opinion or a count of holy sites into a whole number before comparing or coloring it. How it rounds is not documented.

label: Fixed-point to percent
summary: Turns a fixed-point number into a progress percentage by multiplying it by 100, with no limit.
details: A value of 0.5 becomes 50. Unlike CurrentAndMaxToProgressbarValueInt32, the result is not limited to 0 to 100. Vanilla uses it for the maximum clan tax and levies shown in government texts.

label: Make 2D vector
summary: Builds a 2D vector from two decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name, the two numbers become the two components. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Make 3D vector
summary: Builds a 3D vector from three decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name, the three numbers become the three components. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Make 4D vector
summary: Builds a 4D vector from four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name, the four numbers become the four components. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Body available for burial
summary: Whether the deceased character in scope is valid for burial.
details: It asks the scripted GUI 'funeral_is_body_available_gui' with the character as root. Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the funeral activity's deceased selection.

label: Game rule
summary: The game rule a game text is about.
details: Vanilla names it in the list of rules that block achievements, next to its setting, and in a debug condition text.

label: Game rule setting
summary: The chosen setting of a game rule in a game text.
details: Vanilla's one use writes "[rule]: [setting]" in the list of rules that block achievements.

label: Region
summary: The geographical region a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts that add a region to a situation's sub-region.

label: Government type
summary: A government type object that a text can work with.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for a government type. The vanilla lines found write $GOVERNMENT_TYPE|V$, a text variable that the game fills in, not a call of this function, so they do not show how it is used.

label: Graphical unit type
summary: A graphical unit type object that a text can work with.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for how a unit looks on the map. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Great Holy War
summary: The Great Holy War a game text is about.
details: Vanilla names it through its faith's name for such wars, for example when it starts or when a character withdraws a pledge.

label: Great project
summary: The great project (a massive undertaking of a realm, such as building a great building) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's great project texts use it to name the project, its build progress and the days left until it is done.

label: Project contribution
summary: One contribution of a great project that a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's condition texts use it to name a contribution, for example whether it is essential before work on the project can start.

label: Contribution type
summary: The kind of great project contribution a text names.
details: Vanilla's one use is the text that gives a contribution its name, taken from this type.

label: Great project type
summary: The kind of great project a text names.
details: Vanilla builds a project's name from it, alone or after the owner's house name.

label: Has several players
summary: Whether the running game has more than one player.
details: Going by its name and its uses, it is used to decide whether to show who paused the game, and in event windows to show the timeout option. It returns true or false.

label: Is multiplayer
summary: Whether the running game is a multiplayer game.
details: Going by its name and its uses, vanilla uses it in the in-game menu and the multiplayer lobby to show or hide buttons. It returns true or false.

label: Game over text
summary: The description text shown when the game is over.
details: Going by its name and its return type (text), it is the explanation on a game over screen. Vanilla does not use it in the lines found, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Fourth component (decimal)
summary: The 'A' part of a 4D decimal vector, as a decimal number.
details: Going by its name, 'A' is probably the fourth component of the vector (the alpha part if the vector is a color). Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Fourth component (whole)
summary: The 'A' part of a 4D whole-number vector, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name, 'A' is probably the fourth component of the vector (the alpha part if the vector is a color). Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Mouse position
summary: The mouse pointer's position on the screen, as a 2D decimal vector.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it gives the absolute screen position. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Mouse position (whole)
summary: The mouse pointer's position on the screen, as a 2D whole-number vector.
details: Going by its name and its return type, it is the whole-number version of GetAbsoluteMousePosition. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Accolade pose
summary: The name of the pose used to show an accolade's knight in the accolade window.
details: Going by its name and its single use, vanilla hands it to Character.GetPortrait as the pose of the portrait in the accolade window. The result is a text.
